newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK British commander greets Chinese army unit.
newsitem.headline: HK British commander greets Chinese army unit.

text.p: An advance unit of China's People's Liberation Army arrived at the British barracks in central Hong Kong on Monday and was greeted by British commander, Major-General Bryan Dutton.

Dutton exchanged salutes and handshakes with China's Major-General Zhou Borong before leading the party into the Prince of Wales Barracks, where the PLA will prepare garrison facilities for the territory's return to China on July 1.
By coincidence the 40-strong unit drove up to the barracks shortly after the British garrison's annual 21 gun salute in honour of Queen Elizabeth's birthday.
In the yard of the barracks were a handful of men in kilts from Britain's Black Watch regiment, but there were none of the regiment's traditional bagpipe performances and the reception was low-key.

A British spokeswoman said there would be meetings between the PLA and British to discuss arrangements for the Chinese troops, 28 of whom will be billeted at the barracks while 12 will be stationed at a base on nearby Stonecutters' Island.

"I am delighted to welcome Major-General Zhou Borong and his advance party to the British garrison in Hong Kong and to the Prince of Wales Barracks," Dutton said. "We intend to ensure that the garrison gives the PLA every possible assistance in their preparations," he said.
